lines: You cast trouble into the water. Fine. Now reel back something better.
Bad tides pass. I'll see whether you bring the same storm again.
You tangled the line. Fine. Untangle it slowly and do not cut it again.
An apology floats. Trust sinks or holds by what follows.
I'll hear you out. I have waited longer for worse catches.
Bad waters calm if the wind changes. Let us see whether yours does.
You hooked harm and brought it here. Now bring something decent.
Fine. I'll not throw the words back, but I'll inspect them.
I was wrong. I would rather say it plainly than dress it up.
That came out sharper than it should have. I am sorry.
